extracted.intended_audience: applicants for German utility model protection (prospective inventors, attorneys, and representatives)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural requirements for filing and maintaining a Gebrauchsmuster (utility model) application at the German Patent and Trademark Office (DPMA), including required documents, novelty rules, fees, timelines, representation and post‑grant procedures. Focused on practical filing content and formalities specific to Germany/DPMA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differences between utility model and patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical inventions can be protected by both patents and utility models. Please note that technical, chemical and biological processes can be patented but not protected as utility models. The term of protection of utility models is different to that of patents. Utility model protection is initially available for three years. It may be extended to a maximum of ten years. A patent can provide protection for up to twenty years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In case of utility models, substantive requirements for protection such as novelty and inventiveness are initially not examined. An examination is carried out only later within the framework of cancellation or infringement proceedings. This makes utility models easier, faster and cheaper than patents. However, there is a greater risk for utility models to be challenged and cancelled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the official application form (G 6003)
rubrics_metrics.description: Please use the official form (Antrag auf Eintragung eines Gebrauchsmusters - G 6003) when applying for a utility model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application must be filed using the official DPMA form; supporting materials (description, drawings, claims) must accompany this form. Formal requirements for application documents are stipulated by the Utility Model Ordinance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required description contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The description is an essential element of the utility model application. Please describe the following in your text: the state of the art, the problem underlying the invention, the solution to the problem (the invention as such), the advantages of this solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The description can be supplemented by one or multiple technical drawings. The invention must be fully described already in the documents submitted at the date of filing. If you subsequently submit further technical features, the application could be refused due to inadmissible extension. Another legal consequence could be the deferment of the date of filing to the date of the subsequently filed document being received. An example of a description can be found in the DPMA leaflet “Information for Utility Model Applicants”.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must be submitted and determine scope
rubrics_metrics.description: You must also submit claims. The contents of the claims determine the scope of protection of your utility model. Therefore, the wording of the claims is particularly important.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The claims must contain the technical features that are to be protected. Information about the invention’s purpose or advantages does not meet this requirement. For tips on how to draft the claims, refer to the “Information for Utility Model Applicants” leaflet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal requirements per Utility Model Ordinance
rubrics_metrics.description: The formal requirements for the application documents are stipulated by the Utility Model Ordinance (Gebrauchsmusterverordnung).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consult the Ordinance and the DPMA information leaflets to ensure submitted documents meet formal rules (formatting, required sections, signatures, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: State of the art definition and novelty rules (utility model specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: The state of the art is the yardstick of the 'novelty' and 'inventive step' requirements for protection. The state of the art comprises all written publications and any public use that adversely affect novelty of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The definition of ‘state of the art’ in utility model law is stricter than in patent law: only written descriptions are covered (oral descriptions are not covered); public use is prejudicial as to novelty only if it has taken place in Germany. Furthermore, the applicant is granted a grace period of six months: the applicant may make their invention available to the public up to six months prior to filing the application without precluding utility model protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application fee payment timing and amounts
rubrics_metrics.description: An application fee of 40 euros for a utility model application must be paid within three months from filing the application. Otherwise, the application will be deemed to be withdrawn. The application fee is as low as 30 euros for e-filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the DPMA form A 9510 (Information Concerning Costs, Fees and Expenses) for individual fee items and rates applicable to DPMA proceedings. Ensure timely payment to avoid withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance fees and lapse rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintenance fees are due after three, six and eight years. If the respective maintenance fee is not paid at all, not paid in due time or not paid in full, the utility model will lapse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay maintenance fees on schedule (3/6/8 years) to keep protection in force up to the maximum ten‑year term; check DPMA fee pages for amounts and deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration timeline (average)
rubrics_metrics.description: The registration procedure is completed, on average, within 4,0 months (status 2024).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reflects DPMA processing times for registration (not substantive examination); expect faster initial registration than patent prosecution but note later risks (cancellation proceedings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation requirements (residency rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants can apply for IP rights themselves. It is at the applicant's discretion to decide whether to seek the help of a lawyer or patent attorney. However, applicants who do not have their residence in Germany must be represented in respect of the application by a lawyer or patent attorney authorised to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non‑resident applicants must appoint an authorised German representative; consult DPMA page on Legal representation before the DPMA for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal aid availability for financially needy applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: You can request legal aid for a utility model application if your financial circumstances are difficult.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If legal aid is granted, a lawyer or patent attorney can be assigned as your representative. See DPMA leaflet “Merkblatt über Verfahrenskostenhilfe vor dem Deutschen Patent- und Markenamt” for details (in German).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance fee payment processing and confirmation
rubrics_metrics.description: For utility models which are still in force, the next due date is displayed in DPMAregister in the list of master data in the Due date line. If the fee amount has been paid in full and correctly for the file number, the payment is usually processed within the next 35 days and – if admissible – the next due date will be indicated in the corresponding line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computation of the next fee due may be delayed in some cases; the DPMA stopped issuing receipts as of 1 June 2011 — use the updated data of your Register entry as confirmation of payment. Information on fees and fee payment is available on DPMA pages.
